paper_metadata.title: Classical optimization with imaginary time block encoding on quantum computers: The MaxCut problem

summary: The paper proposes two gate-based quantum simulation protocols for MaxCut: pure ITE-BE and QAOA+ITE-BE. On 100 random unweighted 3-regular graphs for N = 6, 8, 10, 12, both methods show approximation ratio and optimal-solution probability increasing toward 1 as imaginary time τ approaches 2, while post-selection success decays exponentially; the hybrid QAOA+ITE-BE improves post-selection by about an order of magnitude at τ = 2 for N = 12. The paper also reports faster convergence on bipartite 3-regular graphs, with post-selection plateaus near τ ≈ 0.6 for pure ITE-BE and τ ≈ 0.4 for QAOA+ITE-BE.

experiments.description: Pure ITE-BE (imaginary-time evolution block encoding) for MaxCut on randomly generated unweighted 3-regular graphs, evaluated by simulation across graph sizes N=6,8,10,12 and imaginary time τ∈[0,2].

algorithm.convergence_criteria: evaluate performance as a function of imaginary time τ up to 2; convergence observed when approximation ratio and optimal-solution probability saturate near 1

problem_formulation.encoding_details: MaxCut on an undirected graph; one data qubit per vertex plus one reusable ancilla qubit; imaginary-time propagator implemented edge-by-edge via block encoding
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize C(s)=1/2 * sum_{<j,k> in E} w_jk (1 - s_j s_k)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: post-selection on ancilla qubit being |0>; for the first layer with |+> initial state, a corrected deterministic block is used to avoid post-selection failure
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_C = - sum_{<j,k> in E} w_jk/2 (I - Z_j Z_k)

problem_instance.description: MaxCut on randomly generated unweighted 3-regular graphs

dataset_specification.description: 100 random instances for each N in {6,8,10,12}; w_jk=1 on every edge

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: For each τ, run 10^5 shots per graph, repeat 10 times, exclude graphs with at least one overall failure across repetitions, and report 99.7% uncertainty intervals for approximation ratio, optimal-solution probability, and post-selection rate

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compute approximation ratio r, optimal-solution probability popt, and post-selection success rate from successful executions

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: r and popt increase monotonically with τ and saturate near 1; post-selection rate decays exponentially with τ
